name: ohmstead

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The signed-in Ohmstead user, plan, and the teams and classes they're in (with their role).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The user's Ohmstead projects, newest first. Personal workspace by default; pass team (name or id, see whoami) for that team's projects you can see.

team.description: Team or class name or id. Omit for your personal projects.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: A project's subsystems, components (tag → Codex part), P&ID items and lines, wires (grid rows) and current issues. Set format=json for the raw document.

tools.name: get_bom
tools.description: The project's bill of materials: devices by Codex part (fuses and breakers per trip rating), terminal strip blocks and accessories, connector housings with their contacts, seals, plugs, backshells and locks, splices, cables by spec with total length, and loose wire by gauge and color with total length. format=csv gives a spreadsheet-ready CSV.

tools.name: export_project_file
tools.description: The project as an Ohmstead project file (.ohmstead): plain text, one line per part and wire, sorted, addressed by tag, with drag positions and draw order in the last section. Commit it to Git or edit it and bring it back with import_project_file. Lines starting with # at the top list references that were left out because what they point at no longer exists.

tools.name: import_project_file
tools.description: Read an Ohmstead project file (.ohmstead text). With project_id it goes over that project: components, subsystems and wires keep their ids by tag, so saved positions and embeds survive. Without apply it only reports what would change (always do that first and show the user); apply=true saves. Without project_id it makes a new project named title (Free plan: max 3). Parts resolve by id, then by maker and number; anything missing or ambiguous is named and nothing is saved.

title.description: Name for a new project (without project_id).

team.description: Team or class for a new project. Omit for your personal workspace.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project (Free plan: max 3, always public). sample=true starts from the sample project (the Arduino Parking Sensor template). Pass team (name or id) to create it in a team or class: it starts private to you and the team's owner/admins; share it from Ohmstead.

team.description: Team or class name or id (you must be an editor/student or up). Omit for your personal workspace.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Rename, change status/visibility (Pro/Student only for private), default signal flow, title block fields, the sizing standard and its ampacity column, the length unit, the voltage-drop limits, or the spare-terminal percentage. title_block keys are the PDF template's field ids (built-in: drawingNo, drawnBy, customer, rev; custom template fields have their own ids).

default_block.description: Terminal block part (id or part number) new strips and strip terminals use when none is picked. null = generic block.

default_pe_block.description: Same, for protective-earth strips. null = generic PE block.

strip_report.description: PDF: a terminal strip report page per strip (default true).

sizing_report.description: PDF: a sizing report page, one section per fuse or breaker (default on when any wire has sizing data).

bom_report.description: PDF: a bill of materials, the last section (default on when the project has anything to list).

pid_sheets.description: PDF: P&ID sheets after the schematic (default on when the project has P&ID items).

strip_naming.description: Tags for new strips: tb = TB1 / TB-PWR1 (default), iec = -X1, -X2. Existing strips keep their tags.

connector_tags.description: Tags for new in-line connectors (category connector): x = X10, X11… (default), jp = J1… for female, P1… for male. Existing ones keep their tags.

pack_on_fix.description: fix_fanouts / Fix all re-pack the strips they touch.

project_type.description: What the project is; sets defaults. vehicle (vehicle / harness): fix_fanouts uses splices; enclosure (cabinet) and electronics: terminal strips. null clears it.

harness_report.description: PDF: a drawing sheet and a breakout table per harness you made (default true). Bundles never print.

pinout_report.description: PDF: a pinout table per mated pair, feed-through and wired unmated connector (default true).

bundle_min.description: Fewest wires between two subsystems that draw as one bundle on screen (one trunk line; it never prints). Default 3; null resets it.

harness_min.description: Deprecated: the old name of bundle_min.

spare_terminal_pct.description: Packing (Clean up, fix_fanouts) appends this many spare terminals per strip, in % of its used terminals (0–50), empty and unlocked at the end. null = none.

gauge_units.description: Wire gauge units in the grid, labels and PDF (default awg). In mm2 projects a bare gauge number means mm².

gauge_on_labels.description: Printed wire labels include the gauge ("24VDC (+) 18 AWG BU"). Default false.

sizing_standard.description: Sizing standard behind gauge and fuse suggestions (default nec). electronics: dev boards, breakouts and header pins, ampacity down to 30 AWG and no minimum size on DC or signal wires.

sizing_column.description: Ampacity / insulation column of the standard (e.g. "75C", "105C-outside"); must be one of its columns. null = the standard's default.

ambient_c.description: Ambient temperature the ampacity is corrected for, in °C (0–100). null = the default 40 °C (inside the enclosure).

length_unit.description: Unit lengths are entered and shown in (default ft). Stored lengths are metres either way.

drop_branch_pct.description: Branch voltage-drop limit — from the last fuse or breaker to the load — in % of the signal's volts (0–100). null = the default 3 %.

drop_total_pct.description: Total voltage-drop limit to the supply, in % of the signal's volts (0–100). null = the default 5 %.

tools.name: add_components
tools.description: Place Codex parts in a project under unique tags (e.g. PLC_MAIN, PSU1, K1); no tag = the next free one for the part's category (in-line connectors: X10… or J1 / P1, see update_project connector_tags). The part must already exist in the Codex (search_codex / save_part). subsystem = name or id of an existing subsystem.

tools.name: update_components
tools.description: Retag a component, relink it to another Codex part, move it into a subsystem (subsystem: name/id, or "" for top level), put an I/O module in a PLC slot (plc + slot; a module already in that slot is taken out), or set a fuse/breaker's trip rating (trip_a; must be one of the part's allowed ratings when it lists any), or pick the contact of an in-line connector's pin by hand (contact_by_pin). Identify by current tag.

plc.description: I/O modules: tag of the PLC whose rack it goes in, or "" to take it out

trip_a_by_terminal.description: Fused circuits (a fuse block, a distributor): the fuse in A per terminal, e.g. {"1": 15, "2": 20}. null clears one.

trip_a.description: Fuse/breaker components: the trip rating in A chosen for this instance. null clears it.

contact_by_pin.description: In-line connectors: contact part (id or part number, category connector, accessory contact) per pin, overriding the pick by wire gauge, e.g. {"3": "GEN-DT-P16-14"}. null = back to automatic.

tools.name: remove_components
tools.description: Delete components (devices or terminal strips) by tag, with every wire and cable on them. Modules in a removed PLC's rack come out of it; linked P&ID items stay and are unlinked. Nothing is deleted if any tag is unknown.

tools.name: add_subsystem
tools.description: Create a subsystem (group) to organize components, optionally nested under a parent subsystem, with its own signal flow.

tools.name: update_subsystem
tools.description: Rename a subsystem, move it under another parent (parent: name/id, or "" for top level; its components and child subsystems come with it), change its signal flow, or mark it as an enclosure (every wire or cable crossing its frame must then pass a feed-through or gland on its wall).

enclosure.description: true = an enclosure (cabinet, box): crossings need a feed-through or gland; false = a plain subsystem

tools.name: split_subsystem
tools.description: Split a subsystem in two: move some of its own components and child subsystems into a new subsystem beside it (same parent, signal flow and collapsed state; not an enclosure). Use it when a collapsed block has too many ports to fit a sheet. Wires and cables don't change; the ones between the two halves run between two blocks. Name what moves with components (tags) and/or subsystems (names or ids), all directly inside the subsystem, or pass half: true to move about half, keeping blocks wired to each other together. At least one member must stay.

subsystem.description: Name or id of the subsystem to split

components.description: Tags of components directly in the subsystem to move

subsystems.description: Names or ids of child subsystems to move (with everything in them)

half.description: true = pick about half automatically, by wiring; don't combine with components / subsystems

tools.name: remove_subsystem
tools.description: Delete a subsystem. Nothing else is deleted: its components and child subsystems move up to its parent (or the top level).

tools.name: layout_view
tools.description: Run the schematic layout for one view (the project, or a subsystem's drill-down) and list every block's position and size and every print page's frame, so blocks and pages can be placed without guessing. Block x, y are relative to the block's own subsystem (what set_block_positions takes); ax, ay are absolute in the view (what pages use). Pages are a fixed 1504 × 800 frame; automatic pages (auto:0, auto:1…) cover whatever no placed page holds. Takes a few seconds, up to ~15 s on a large project.

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tools.name: set_block_positions
tools.description: Pin blocks (components, terminal strips or subsystems) at positions in one view, instead of where auto-layout puts them. x, y are the block's top-left, relative to its own subsystem in that view (layout_view shows current values). Unpinned blocks keep laying out automatically. Wires reroute in the app.

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tag.description: Component tag, subsystem name, or a node id from layout_view (reference flags are x:…)

tools.name: clear_block_positions
tools.description: Unpin every block in one view so it goes back to auto-layout. Other views keep theirs.

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tools.name: add_page
tools.description: Place a print page: a fixed 1504 × 800 frame in one view with its top-left at x, y (absolute view coordinates, as layout_view's ax, ay and frames). Blocks whose centre is inside print on it; the rest go on automatic pages after the placed ones. Pages print in the order they were added within each view.

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Rename or move a print page. page: id or name of a placed page, or an automatic page "auto:0", "auto:1"… (with subsystem for a drill-down view; automatic pages can only be renamed, and an empty name gives back the automatic one).

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tools.name: remove_page
tools.description: Remove a placed print page (id or name). Its blocks stay where they are and print on automatic pages.

subsystem.description: Subsystem whose drill-down view this is (name or id). Omit for the project view.

tools.name: add_terminal_strip
tools.description: Add a terminal strip (auto-tagged TB1, TB2…). Usually fix_fanouts creates strips for you; use this for planned strips. Its terminals use `block` if given, else the project default block, else a generic block (terminal_type, clamps_per_side).

block.description: Terminal block part for this strip: part id or part number, or "PE" for the project's PE block. Omit for the project default.

tools.name: add_splice
tools.description: Add splices (auto-tagged SP1, SP2…): one-conductor joints like a terminal strip, created on demand. Every wire lands on SP1:1 and a splice takes any number of wires. Usually fix_fanouts via "splice" creates them for you. part = a Codex splice part (id or part number, category splice) whose wire range and most wires validate_project checks; omit for a generic splice. Remove one with remove_components.

part.description: Splice part id or part number (category splice). Omit for a generic splice.

tools.name: set_strip_blocks
tools.description: Set the terminal block part of strip terminals (a range by label, or all). Wires keep their level: bare labels become level A on a multi-level block and back. Refused if wires sit on a level the new block doesn't have. block = part id or part number; omit (null) to return the terminals to the strip default.

tools.name: optimize_strips
tools.description: Re-pack terminal strips to the fewest terminals: each net becomes one jumpered run sized to its wires (block capacity), empty spares go, like signals sit together, unlocked terminals are renumbered 1..n (locked ones keep their numbers). Multi-level and diode/LED blocks, cabled nets, and nets whose wires don't fit a run's clamp range (block wire_mm2) are left as they are. With spare_terminal_pct set (update_project), each packed strip ends with that share of its used terminals as empty spare terminals. Device connections never change. apply=false (default) only reports the before/after counts; ask the user before applying, since terminal numbers change.

strip.description: Strip tag; omit for every strip

tools.name: split_strips
tools.description: Split strips so each serves one subsystem and/or one function: power (TB-PWR), PE (TB-PE), AC (TB-AC), field I/O per PLC module (TB-IO); the rest stays on plain TB strips. Everything tied together on a strip moves as one unit; a unit serving several subsystems goes to their common parent (shared distribution at the level above). Wires move with their terminals; device connections never change. apply=false (default) reports the plan; ask the user before applying. pack=true also re-packs the results (like optimize_strips).

strip.description: Strip tag; omit for every strip

tools.name: set_strip_parts
tools.description: Override how many of a part a strip needs (accessories: end plates, end stops, jumper bars, markers, or any extra part). Ohmstead works these out from the blocks; an override replaces that count (0 removes the part). qty null = back to the worked-out count. Block counts can't be overridden; change the terminals instead.

tools.name: add_connections
tools.description: Append wires (grid rows) between component terminals. Terminals must exist on the Codex part; terminal strips accept new terminal labels. Returns the issues after the change.

signal.description: Signal type name or id. Default: the From terminal's Codex signal.

draw.description: auto (default), force a drawn wire, or force reference flags

gauge.description: Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

harness.description: Harness tag (H1) or name to build this loose wire into; text that names no harness makes one ("rear loom" becomes H<n> named rear loom). A harness prints and its conductors count together to derate ampacity. "" takes it out. A cable conductor is in its cable's harness (update_cable harness).

bundle.description: Deprecated: the old name of harness.

length.description: Wire length in the project's length unit (ft default, or m; update_project length_unit), for the voltage-drop check. null clears it. Cable conductors inherit the cable's length.

tools.name: update_connection
tools.description: Change one wire (grid row) by id: either end, signal, note, draw mode, gauge, harness, or length (in the project's unit; null clears). Omitted fields stay the same; note "" clears it, gauge "" goes back to the signal type's gauge, harness "" takes it out of its harness.

signal.description: Signal type name or id. Default: the From terminal's Codex signal.

draw.description: auto (default), force a drawn wire, or force reference flags

gauge.description: Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

harness.description: Harness tag (H1) or name to build this loose wire into; text that names no harness makes one ("rear loom" becomes H<n> named rear loom). A harness prints and its conductors count together to derate ampacity. "" takes it out. A cable conductor is in its cable's harness (update_cable harness).

bundle.description: Deprecated: the old name of harness.

length.description: Wire length in the project's length unit (ft default, or m; update_project length_unit), for the voltage-drop check. null clears it. Cable conductors inherit the cable's length.

tools.name: remove_connections
tools.description: Remove wires (grid rows) from a project by id. This edits the project; it never deletes projects or Codex parts.

tools.name: add_cable
tools.description: Add a multi-conductor cable between two connectors, e.g. from "B1:X1" to "IO1:X2". Pins are mapped 1:1 (same pin names, else pin order) unless conductors are given. Tag defaults to the next free W1, W2…

spec.description: Printed on the cable, e.g. "4×0.34 PUR 5m"

gauge.description: Default gauge for its conductors. Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

length.description: Cable length in the project's length unit (ft default, or m; update_project length_unit). Its conductors inherit it. null = unset.

from_pin.description: Pin name on the From connector, e.g. "1"

to_pin.description: Pin name on the To connector

signal.description: Signal type name or id. Default: the From pin's Codex signal.

color.description: Conductor color, IEC code or name (BN, WH, BU, BK, GN/YE…)

gauge.description: Conductor gauge; default the cable's gauge, then the signal type's. Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

harness.description: Harness tag (H1) or name to build the cable into; text that names no harness makes one. Its conductors count with the harness's other wires for derating.

bundle.description: Deprecated: the old name of harness.

tools.name: mate_connectors
tools.description: Plug two connectors together: an in-line connector and its other half ("X10" and "X11"), or an in-line connector on a device's connector ("X10" and "PLC1:X1"). Mated pins are one conductor, 1:1 (same pin names, else pin order) unless pins are given. Each connector can be in one mate. Gender, keying and pin counts are checked by validate_project.

tools.name: unmate_connectors
tools.description: Unplug a mate: name either of its connectors ("X10" or "TAG:CONNECTOR") or its id from get_project. The connectors and their wires stay.

tools.name: get_pinouts
tools.description: Pinout tables, as printed in the PDF: each mate with both halves side by side, each feed-through with its two sides, and each unmated connector that has wiring. Per cavity: signal, wire (cable or harness tag), color, gauge, contact and seal or cavity plug (in-line housings), and the far end. Name a connector ("X10", "PLC1:X1") for its table only; omit for all.

connector.description: "X10", "TAG:CONNECTOR", or a feed-through tag; omit for every table

tools.name: assign_gland
tools.description: Put a cable, or a loose wire, through a cable gland on an enclosure wall (G2): gland "GL1", or null to take it out. One cable per gland; loose wires may share a gland but not with a cable. Set the cable's outer diameter with update_cable od_mm so validate_project can check it fits.

gland.description: Gland tag (GL1), or null to clear

wire.description: A loose wire: its id from get_project, or "FROM:TERM -> TO:TERM"

tools.name: update_harness
tools.description: Harnesses (H1, H2…) are assemblies you make and someone builds: a tag, a name, a part number and the loose wires and cables built into them. They print (tagged trunk, drawing sheet, breakout table, BOM line) and their current-carrying conductors, cables' included, count together to derate ampacity. Create one (omit harness, give a new H tag, or from_bundle to start from a bundle's wires), add or remove wires (ids from get_project) and cables (tags), retag, name it, set its part number, draw it as a trunk or as separate wires (everywhere or in one view), or delete it (its wires and cables stay). A wire or cable is in one harness at most: adding it moves it. A cable conductor id stands for its cable.

harness.description: Harness tag (H1) or name. Omit, or give a tag no harness has, to create one.

part_number.description: Part or drawing number of the built harness, for the BOM and its drawing sheet. null clears it.

from_bundle.description: Bundle tag (B1) or key from get_project: its wires go into the harness (a new one unless harness names one).

add_wires.description: Wire ids to put in it

add_cables.description: Cable tags or ids to put in it

show.description: One trunk or separate wires, in every view.

view.description: Subsystem name or id for view_show; null = the top-level view.

view_show.description: Trunk or separate wires in that view; null goes back to `show`.

tools.name: update_bundle
tools.description: Screen overrides for a bundle: all loose wires between the same two subsystems (or a subsystem and a terminal strip), worked out automatically and drawn on screen as one line with a tag (B1, B2…). Bundles never print (the PDF draws those wires separately) and don't derate. get_project lists them. Retag, name it, draw it as a trunk or as separate wires, everywhere or in one view, change its minimum wire count, or make it one multi-core cable (promote). null clears a field back to automatic. The project-wide minimum is update_project bundle_min. To make a bundle's wires a harness that prints, use update_harness from_bundle.

bundle.description: Bundle tag (B1) or key from get_project

show.description: Trunk or separate wires, in every view.

view.description: With view_show: a subsystem name or id to set it for, or null for the top level.

view_show.description: Trunk or separate wires in that view; null goes back to `show`.

min_wires.description: Fewest wires for this pair to draw as a bundle.

promote.description: These wires really are one multi-core cable: they become conductors of a new W-tagged cable landing on the same terminals.

spec.description: With promote: the cable spec, e.g. "4×0.75 PUR"

tools.name: update_cable
tools.description: Change a cable by tag or id: retag, spec, gauge, length, outer diameter (od_mm), either end (the pin map resets to 1:1), replace the whole pin map (conductors), reset it (reset_pin_map), set the draw mode, or build it into a harness. Omitted fields stay the same.

gauge.description: Default gauge for its conductors; "" clears it. Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

length.description: Cable length in the project's length unit; its conductors inherit it. null clears it.

od_mm.description: Outer diameter in mm, checked against the gland it passes (assign_gland). null clears it.

from_pin.description: Pin name on the From connector, e.g. "1"

to_pin.description: Pin name on the To connector

signal.description: Signal type name or id. Default: the From pin's Codex signal.

color.description: Conductor color, IEC code or name (BN, WH, BU, BK, GN/YE…)

gauge.description: Conductor gauge; default the cable's gauge, then the signal type's. Wire gauge: AWG ("18", "14 AWG", "1/0") or mm² ("1.5 mm²"). A bare number follows the project's gauge units. Default: the signal type's gauge.

harness.description: Harness tag (H1) or name to build it into (text that names no harness makes one); "" takes it out.

bundle.description: Deprecated: the old name of harness.

tools.name: remove_cable
tools.description: Remove a cable and its conductors from a project (the connectors stay on their parts). A terminal-end cable's conductors stay as loose wires. This edits the project; it never deletes projects or Codex parts.

tools.name: add_pid_items
tools.description: Add symbols to the project's P&ID (list_pid_symbols has the keys). With no tag an item gets the next free one (I-1, V-1, P-1, TK-1, E-1; actuators get none). With no position the auto-layout places it. size is for equipment only and snaps to the symbol's 10-unit steps. With component, the item links to that wiring component and the project's tag rule decides what it prints, so the result shows the printed tag.

tag.description: ISA tag, e.g. "FT-101". On note.text and area.frame, the words it shows.

at.description: Top-left of the item's box. A port sits at x + w/2 + its x offset, y + h/2 + its y offset (list_pid_symbols has the offsets), so level ports need different y on items of different heights.

component.description: Tag of the wiring component to link

location.description: Where the instrument sits; sets its ISA bubble

props.description: Free fields: size, range, set point, fail position…

tools.name: update_pid_items
tools.description: Change placed P&ID items without touching their lines: position, size, symbol, tag, location, props. Lines keep their spot through a resize or symbol change. A tag follows the project's tag rule: renaming an item linked under the "same" rule renames its wiring component too. A blank location unsets it, and so does a blank props field.

tools.name: add_process_lines
tools.description: Draw lines between P&ID items. from and to are "TAG:PORT" or "TAG" (tag or item id; list_pid_symbols has each symbol's ports, and a bare side like 90 on a side with several ports takes the one closest to the other end, so the line runs straight when a port lines up; with no positions, the one closest to the side's centre). kind defaults to process. Signal lines come from the wiring, so draw one only for something not wired yet. A line from an item to itself or an exact duplicate is skipped.

label.description: Line number or pipe spec, e.g. 2"-CW-101-A1

tools.name: link_instrument
tools.description: Link a P&ID item to a wiring component by tag, or clear the link with component null. The project's tag rule decides which tag the item prints, and the result shows it.

component.description: Wiring component tag, or null to clear the link

tools.name: remove_pid_items
tools.description: Remove items from the P&ID, and every line touching them. Linked wiring components stay in the schematic.

tools.name: remove_process_lines
tools.description: Remove lines from the P&ID by id (get_project lists them). Signal lines derived from the wiring aren't stored here; change the wiring to change them.

tools.name: add_pid_sheet
tools.description: Add a named print sheet to the P&ID: a frame of 1504 × 800 units with its top-left at x,y. An item prints on the sheet holding its centre, sheets print in the order listed, and items outside every sheet tile onto automatic sheets after them. The result lists what each sheet holds.

tools.name: update_pid_sheet
tools.description: Rename a placed P&ID sheet, move its frame (x,y is the top-left), or change where it prints (position, 1 = first). sheet is its id or name. The result lists what each sheet holds.

position.description: Place in print order among the placed sheets

tools.name: remove_pid_sheet
tools.description: Remove a placed P&ID sheet by id or name. Its items stay on the drawing and move to the automatic sheets.

tools.name: list_pid_symbols
tools.description: P&ID symbols by group: key, label, base size, whether it resizes, and its ports with their x,y offset from the item's centre at that size. A resized item's ports are listed when it is added.

tools.name: validate_project
tools.description: Check a project for fan-outs (too many wires on a terminal), signal clashes (different signal types on one net), incomplete rows, missing signals, and terminals/parts that don't exist. Also reports supply overloads, wires outside their terminal block's clamp wire range, and sizing findings (wire too small, below the minimum size, fuse too big, missing fuse rating, voltage drop over the limit) with suggested values from the project's sizing standard. Info notes list relays, I/O, e-stops, breakers, PSUs and motors whose Codex part has no function (or incomplete terminal roles) yet, so they draw as plain blocks.

tools.name: explain_sizing
tools.description: One wire's sizing breakdown — current, design current, gauge, ampacity and its derating, voltage drop, the fuse or breaker behind it, and the suggested gauge — the same numbers the wire's details show in Ohmstead. Find the wire by id, or by its ends like update_connection takes them.

tools.name: fix_fanouts
tools.description: Route every fan-out through terminal strips (one strip per electrical net, jumpered as needed), same as the app's "Fix all". via defaults to the project type (splices in a vehicle project, else strips). New strips use the project default block (update_project default_block); protective-earth fan-outs get the PE block (default_pe_block, else a generic PE block). terminal_type only applies to generic blocks. via "splice" routes device fan-outs through splices (SP1…, one per net) instead; over-full strip terminals always stay on their strip.

via.description: Route fan-outs through terminal strips or splices; omit for the project type's default

tools.name: allow_multiple_wires
tools.description: Let one device terminal take several wires in this project (e.g. a two-level terminal), silencing its fan-out. allow=false reverts.

tools.name: search_codex
tools.description: Search the parts library (built-in, community and yours) by name, part number, manufacturer, description or terminal name.

category.description: One of: device, plc, psu, battery, relay, terminal, estop, io, hmi, breaker, motor, sensor, resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, connector, splice, gland

tools.name: list_signal_types
tools.description: Signal types (name, category, wire color, gauge, volts) available for terminals and wires.

tools.name: save_signal_type
tools.description: Create a signal type (what a wire carries and the color it draws in), or update one you own (pass signal_id). Comms types draw dashed and let a terminal take several wires without a fan-out. Free users' signal types are always public; Pro ones default to private. Built-in types are read-only.

stripe_color.description: Tracer stripe as hex, or null for none

dashed.description: Draw dashed (cables / comms). Default: true for comms

awg.description: Default wire gauge, AWG: "18", "14", "1/0". null clears it.

mm2.description: Default wire gauge as a cross-section in mm², e.g. 0.75. null clears it. Set either or both.

volts.description: Nominal voltage of this signal, e.g. 24 or 120; the voltage-drop check divides by it. null clears it (no drop check).

phases.description: 1 for DC and single-phase (the default), 3 for three-phase (√3 in the drop formula). null clears it (treated as 1).

tools.name: list_manufacturers
tools.description: Manufacturers available for Codex parts.

tools.name: save_part
tools.description: Create a Codex part, or update one you own (pass part_id). A part must be complete: name, manufacturer, part number, category, description and at least one terminal (accessory parts, block.kind accessory, need none). A part can say what it does (function) and what each terminal is to it (terminal role / channel); a part with a function must have every role it needs or the save is refused. Mixed parts (a PLC CPU with onboard DI and AI) list groups, each with its own function, and put terminals in them. Terminal blocks (category terminal) carry block data and per-terminal level/side; terminals can carry load_a / rated_a current data, and protective parts (fuse, breaker) list their allowed trip_ratings. Passive parts (category resistor, capacitor, inductor or diode) with exactly two terminals and no connectors draw on the schematic as inline glyphs, not blocks. Ask the user for datasheet values rather than guessing. On update the terminal list REPLACES the existing one, so include every terminal (use add_part_terminals to just add some). Free users' parts are always public; Pro parts default to private. Pass team (name or id) to create it in that team's Codex (team-only; any editor in the team can edit it later). A part using one of your own signal types in a team needs that signal type in the team too.

team.description: New parts: team or class whose Codex it goes in. Ignored on update (a part stays where it is).

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer name, short code or id (see list_manufacturers)

category.description: One of: device, plc, psu, battery, relay, terminal, estop, io, hmi, breaker, motor, sensor, resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, connector, splice, gland

slot_count.description: PLCs: number of I/O module slots

trip_ratings.description: Protective parts (fuse, breaker): trip ratings in A it can be set to, e.g. [1, 2, 4, 6, 10]. null or [] clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

name.description: Terminal name, or the pin name when connector is set ("1" in X1)

connector.description: Connector this terminal is a pin of, e.g. "X1". Omit for a loose terminal.

signal.description: Default signal type name or id

load_a.description: Current this terminal draws in A (coil, sensor, motor FLA, VFD input). null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

rated_a.description: The most this terminal supplies or carries in A (PSU output, contact rating). null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

through.description: The terminal this one is joined to inside the part, so current passes between them: a switch's other stud, a shunt's other side, a bus bar's other end, a fuse block's common. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

through_fused.description: The through link has its own fuse, sized per circuit (update_components trip_a_by_terminal): a fuse block circuit, a distributor's fused output. Omit to keep what's stored.

fuse_a.description: The fuse the maker specifies for the wire feeding this terminal, in A (datasheet value). Sizing suggests it ahead of any calculation. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

charge_a.description: Current a charger pushes into this terminal's net in A (solar controller or DC-DC output, both polarities). Sizes its wires; never a load on the supply. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

level.description: Terminal blocks: level A/B/C on a multi-level block. Terminals on one level are one conductor. Omit to keep what's stored.

side.description: Terminal blocks: which side of the block this clamp is on. Omit to keep what's stored.

role.description: What this terminal is to the part's function (or its group's): coil_a1/coil_a2 (or coil_in for a relay board's IN pin that drives an onboard coil), no/nc/com contacts, ch_in/ch_common channel terminals, supply_pos/supply_neg, led_a/led_k, out_c/out_e. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

channel.description: Channel number for ch_in / ch_common (AI0 = 0) and coil_in (IN1 = 1, matching its contacts' pole), pole number for no / nc / com (11/12/14 = 1). null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

group.description: Terminal group (from groups) this terminal belongs to, for a mixed part such as a PLC CPU's onboard DI. null = the part's own function; omit to keep what's stored.

connectors.description: Gender / keying per connector named by the terminals. Omit to keep what's stored.

name.description: Connector name used by the terminals, e.g. "X1"

coding.description: Keying / coding, e.g. "A" for M12 A-coded

layout.description: Insert layout: where each cavity sits on the mating face, for harness drawings. A pattern for the male face (mirrored automatically for female): dsub (standard D-sub numbering), grid or ring (generic: match the maker's drawing; ring numbers clockwise from the top, center last). Pins named 1…N go to their numbered position, other names take positions in order. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored (a gender change re-mirrors it).

numbering.description: rows: 1,2,3 across each row; columns: down each column (pin headers, odd/even); u: back along each next row

kind.description: feedthrough, pe, fuse, disconnect, diode, led, sensor, other; or accessory for end plates, end stops, jumper bars, markers

pitch_mm.description: Block width on the DIN rail

wire_mm2.description: Wire range per clamp [min, max] in mm²

jumper.description: plugin = center-slot jumper (uses no clamp), screw = uses a clamp

accessory.description: kind accessory only. Terminal parts: end_plate, end_stop, jumper, marker. Connector parts: contact, seal (both with wire_mm2), cavity_plug, backshell, lock. Gland parts (category gland): gland

passthrough.description: Feed-through (category connector, kind other): its two connectors, inside and outside, are pin N to pin N

cable_od_mm.description: Cable gland (category gland, kind accessory, accessory gland): cable outer diameter range [min, max] in mm

accessories.description: Accessory part ids this block uses

jumpers.description: Pole count → jumper part id, e.g. {"2": "<id>", "10": "<id>"}

contacts.description: Connector housings: contact part ids it takes; each pin gets the tightest one whose wire_mm2 fits its wire

seals.description: Connector housings: wire seal part ids, picked per wired cavity like contacts. Omit for integral seals

cavity_plug.description: Connector housings: plug for each empty cavity

lock.description: Connector housings: secondary lock / wedgelock, one per connector

anyOf.description: Terminal blocks (category terminal), a splice part (category splice: kind other with wire_mm2 and max_conductors = most wires), or connector parts (category connector): a housing is kind other with accessories {contacts, seals, cavity_plug, backshell, lock} and wire_mm2 only for its own field-wireable clamps; a contact, seal, cavity plug, backshell or lock is kind accessory with no terminals. A feed-through is a connector housing (kind other) with passthrough true and two connectors; a cable gland is category gland, kind accessory, accessory gland, cable_od_mm, no terminals. Pass null to clear; omit to keep what's stored.

function.description: What the part does, beside its category: analog_in, analog_out, digital_in, digital_out, relay, contactor, ssr, optocoupler, switch, pushbutton, estop, fuse, breaker, psu, motor, vfd, safety_relay, overload_relay, battery, plain (checked, draws as a plain block on purpose). Its terminals then need roles (a relay: coil_a1 + coil_a2, or coil_in on a relay board, + com with no/nc; a channel card: one ch_in per channel). Only set it from the datasheet. null clears it; omit to keep what's stored.

groups.description: Terminal groups with their own function. Replaces the stored groups; omit to keep them.

name.description: Group name used by the terminals, e.g. "DI" or "AI"

tools.name: add_part_terminals
tools.description: Add terminals to a Codex part. Terminals can carry load_a / rated_a current data (datasheet values, not guesses) and a role / channel / group; the part's other data stays as it is, and a part with a function is checked again for the roles it needs. Your own parts, and team parts in a team where you're an editor or up, are changed in place; anything else is forked into your Codex first (into the team's Codex when project_id is a team project). Pass project_id to relink that project's components to the fork.

tools.name: fork_part
tools.description: Copy a built-in or community part into your own Codex so you can edit it.

tools.name: import_wiring_list
tools.description: Import an existing design into a NEW Ohmstead project. Sources: rows you extracted yourself (read an EPLAN / SKYCAD / AutoCAD Electrical / SolidWorks Electrical PDF page by page: devices with tags + part numbers from the parts list, wires as TAG:TERMINAL pairs from the cross-references / wire numbers, strips with their terminal order from the terminal diagrams), and/or CSV text: wire_csv (connection / wire list export) and bom_csv (BOM / parts list). Devices are matched to the Codex by part number; unknown part numbers are PROPOSED, never created unless listed in accept_parts. BOM lines no wire touches and no Codex part matches (enclosure, hardware) are listed, not placed. Strip numbers are imported locked. level: as-drawn (strips exactly as imported), light (pack, numbers kept), split-pack (split by subsystem + function, pack, numbers kept), full (split, pack, renumber). Device connections are checked to stay identical. Devices with no subsystem hint get PROPOSED subsystems from strip function and how they connect (Power, Control, field groups, areas from numbered tags), never applied unless listed in accept_subsystems; to change one, set subsystem on those device rows and run the dry run again. apply=false (default) returns the report only; show it to the user and ask before applying.

team.description: Team or class name or id to create the project in. Omit for your personal workspace.

tag.description: Device tag as drawn; IEC designations allowed (=PUMP+CP1-K1)

subsystem.description: Subsystem hint: IEC function, BOM section, page group

signal.description: Potential / signal name as drawn (24VDC, 0V, PE, L1…)

strips.description: Terminal order per strip from terminal diagrams

wire_csv.description: Wire / connection list CSV text (EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical, SolidWorks Electrical exports; columns found by name)

bom_csv.description: BOM / parts list CSV text (tag, part number, manufacturer, description, section)

column_map.description: Override column names, e.g. {"fromTag": "Start device", "partNumber": "Order no"}

accept_parts.description: Proposed part numbers to create in the user's Codex before importing (["all"] for every proposal whose manufacturer exists)

accept_subsystems.description: Proposed subsystem names to apply (["all"] for every one). Devices left out stay at project level.

instructions:
Ohmstead is electrical CAD software for wiring schematics: the project is data (parts and wire rows) and the drawing is generated from it.

Model:
- A project has components (device instances with a unique tag like PLC_MAIN, PSU1, K1), each linked to a Codex part.
- The Codex is the shared parts library. A part has a name, manufacturer, part number, category, description and terminals (each with a terminal type, a default signal type, and optional load_a / rated_a current in A; protective parts also list their allowed trip ratings). Parts are only created in the Codex (save_part), never invented inside a project. Signal types too (save_signal_type); check list_signal_types first. Search before creating; built-in and community parts can be forked.
- Wires are grid rows: "FROM_TAG:TERMINAL" → "TO_TAG:TERMINAL" with a signal type (e.g. 24VDC (+), 0VDC (-), Protective Earth). If no signal is given, the From terminal's Codex default is used.
- A device terminal takes one wire unless its Codex terminal allows more (max_wires), the user allowed it, or all wires are comms (daisy-chain). Extra wires are a "fan-out": route them through a terminal strip (TB1, TB2…) with fix_fanouts. Strips are project-level, not Codex parts; their terminals are created on demand.
- Splices (SP1, SP2…) are project-level joints like strips: one conductor, every wire lands on "SP1:1", any number of wires. fix_fanouts via "splice" routes fan-outs through splices instead of strips (the default in a project of type vehicle; update_project project_type); add_splice adds one by hand. A splice can name a Codex part of category splice (butt splice, solder sleeve; save_part with block kind other, wire_mm2 and max_conductors): validate_project flags wires outside its range and more wires than it takes.
- Terminal blocks: Codex parts with category terminal can carry block data (kind, width, wire range, ratings, jumper style, accessory parts) and per-terminal level (A/B/C) and side (in/out). End plates, end stops, jumper bars and markers are accessory parts (block.kind accessory, no terminals). On a strip, each terminal is a block (strip default, project default or a generic block); multi-level blocks are addressed with a level letter: TB1:4A, TB1:4B. Set the project's default block and PE block with update_project (default_block, default_pe_block); fix_fanouts and add_terminal_strip use them. Change blocks on existing terminals with set_strip_blocks. A block's wire range is enforced: validate_project flags wires whose gauge is too big or small for the clamp they land on, and packing leaves such nets where they are. Packing can append spare terminals: update_project spare_terminal_pct sets how many, as a % of each strip's used terminals.
- Subsystems group components and can nest; each has a signal flow (LR or TB). update_subsystem renames one, moves it under another parent or changes its flow; remove_subsystem deletes it and moves its contents up a level. split_subsystem moves some of its members into a new subsystem beside it (for a collapsed block too big for a sheet); wires stay. update_components moves components between subsystems; remove_components deletes them with their wires.
- Connectors: a Codex part's terminals can be grouped into named connectors (X1, X2…), each pin with its own type and default signal, plus gender (male/female) and keying (e.g. M12 A). A pin is addressed "TAG:X1.3" in wires. Give terminals a connector in save_part / add_part_terminals.
- Harnesses (H1, H2…): assemblies you make and someone builds: a tag, a name, a part number and the loose wires and cables built into them (update_harness, or the harness field of add_connections / update_connection / add_cable / update_cable: a tag or name, where unknown text makes a new harness). A harness prints as a tagged trunk with a drawing sheet, a breakout table and a BOM line, and its current-carrying conductors, cables' included, count together to derate ampacity. update_harness from_bundle makes one from a bundle's wires. get_project lists them.
- Bundles (B1, B2…): worked out automatically. All loose wires between the same two subsystems, or a subsystem and a terminal strip, draw as one trunk line on screen once there are enough of them (update_project bundle_min, default 3). They never print (the PDF draws those wires separately) and don't derate. get_project lists them; update_bundle sets screen overrides or makes one a cable. A wire set to draw as a reference stays one, and a wire in a harness leaves its bundle.
- Cables (W1, W2…) join two connectors pin for pin (add_cable). Pins map 1:1 by default (same pin names, else pin order); each conductor is its own row with a signal and an optional conductor color (BN, WH, BU…). Edit with update_cable. Validation flags mated ends with the same gender or different keying. Loose wires may still land on single pins.
- In-line connectors: a Codex part in category connector is one housing (all its terminals in one connector, with gender and keying). Placed in a project it hangs free, anywhere (tagged X10, X11…, or J1 / P1 by gender with update_project connector_tags jp), and its pins are addressed by pin alone: "X10:3". mate_connectors plugs two connectors together ("X10" ↔ "X11", or "X10" ↔ "PLC1:X1"); mated pin N is one conductor with pin N (or a pin map), so nets, current, voltage drop and signal checks pass through. A mate isn't a wire: each pin still takes its own. Cables can end on an in-line connector. A mated connector is a harness end, so a run through a mate is two harnesses. Validation flags mates with the same gender, different keying or different pin counts, and in-line connectors with wiring but no mate. unmate_connectors undoes one; get_project lists mates. get_pinouts gives the pinout tables (each mate side by side, feed-throughs, wired unmated connectors) with signal, wire, color, gauge, contact, seal and far end per cavity; the PDF prints the same (update_project pinout_report).
- Contacts: a connector housing lists the accessory parts it takes (save_part block kind other, accessories: contacts, seals, cavity_plug, backshell, lock); each is a Codex part of category connector, block kind accessory, no terminals, and contacts and seals carry a wire range (wire_mm2). Field-wireable housings with their own clamps give block.wire_mm2 instead. Per pin, the tightest contact (and seal) that fits the wire's gauge is picked; update_components contact_by_pin sets one by hand. Empty cavities get the cavity plug; backshell and lock count once per connector. validate_project flags a wire no contact fits; get_project lists the picked contacts and the parts per connector.
- Enclosures (bulkheads): update_subsystem enclosure true marks a subsystem as an enclosure (a cabinet, a box). Every wire or cable crossing its frame must pass its wall: land on a feed-through (a Codex connector part with passthrough and two connectors, inside and outside, e.g. IN and OUT; pins are "X20:IN.3" / "X20:OUT.3", inside pin N is outside pin N, so nets, current and checks pass through like a mate) or go through a cable gland (a Codex part of category gland, no terminals, block {kind accessory, accessory gland, cable_od_mm [min, max]}). Feed-throughs and glands sit on the wall when placed directly in the enclosure subsystem; glands are tagged GL1…. assign_gland puts a cable (one cable per gland) or loose wires (they may share one) through a gland; set the cable's outer diameter with update_cable od_mm. validate_project flags each crossing with neither, a cable OD outside its gland's range, and a gland that isn't on a wall or isn't crossed. Projects with no enclosure are not checked. get_project lists enclosures and their crossings.
- PLC racks: a PLC part (category plc) can have module slots (slot_count). I/O modules are separate Codex parts (category io). In a project, put a module in a PLC slot with update_components (plc + slot).
- Sizing: projects pick a sizing standard (NEC by default, NFPA 79, ABYC E-11 DC for vehicles, vans and boats, or Low-voltage electronics for dev boards, breakouts and header pins), an ampacity column and an ambient temperature (update_project sizing_standard / sizing_column / ambient_c, default 40 °C); validate_project reports wires too small for their current, minimum sizes and fuse ratings with suggested values, from tables labelled "unverified tables" until the owner checks them. Ampacity is derated for bundling: the conductors of a cable count together, and so do all the conductors of a bundle. Voltage drop (set lengths on wires and cables in the project's length unit, volts and phases on signal types, and the drop limits with update_project) is checked along each wire's run to the supply and flags wires over the branch or total limit; explain_sizing walks through any one wire's numbers (current, derating, drop, the fuse behind it, the suggestion).
- P&ID: a project can carry a process view of the same document. Items are symbols from list_pid_symbols (add_pid_items); process lines join them (add_process_lines); update_pid_items moves, resizes or retags a placed item and its lines stay on. Ports are named by angle in the symbol's own frame, clockwise from up: 0, 90, 180, 270, and 90.1, 90.2 on a side with several. link_instrument ties an item to a wiring component, and the project's tag rule decides which tag it prints. An instrument's signal lines are derived from the wiring, so never add them by hand: wire the component and they appear. A hand-drawn signal line is only for something not wired yet, and validate_project flags it once the wiring disagrees. For words on the drawing use symbols note.text and area.frame, with the words as the tag and an at position: a note wraps to its width, an area is a labelled outline behind the drawing (room boundaries, skids) that prints on every sheet it crosses, and neither takes lines. add_pid_sheet places a named print sheet: a fixed frame that prints the items whose centres it holds; everything else tiles onto automatic sheets.
- Schematic layout and pages: the drawing lays out automatically unless blocks are pinned. layout_view shows a view's blocks (position, size) and print pages; set_block_positions pins blocks, clear_block_positions unpins a whole view. A print page is a fixed-size frame placed in a view (add_page, update_page, remove_page); blocks whose centre is inside print on it, and everything else tiles onto automatic pages (auto:0, auto:1…), which update_page can name. Each subsystem's drill-down is its own view (subsystem).
- Bill of materials: get_bom lists everything to buy (devices by Codex part, strip blocks and accessories, connector housings and contacts, splices, cables by spec with length, loose wire by gauge and color with length), as a table or CSV; get_project ends with the same table. Lengths add up the lengths set on wires and cables.
- Import: import_wiring_list turns an existing design (a PDF you read page by page, a wire-list CSV, a BOM) into a new project; dry run first, then apply after the user agrees.
- Layout, routing and PDF are automatic in the app; the user opens the project in Ohmstead to see the drawing.

Workflow: list_projects / get_project → search_codex → add_components → add_connections → validate_project → fix_fanouts. Report issues to the user rather than guessing; ask before creating Codex parts with uncertain terminal data.
Changes are saved straight to the database. If the project is open in Ohmstead, the user should reload it to see them.
 - Teams and classes: whoami lists the user's teams and their role (classes say instructor / TA / student / viewer). list_projects, create_project, save_part and import_wiring_list take an optional team (name or id); every other tool follows the project's team. A team project is visible to its creator, the team's owner/admins and members it's shared with. Submitted / issued (locked) projects are read-only, and so is a project a teammate has open for editing in Ohmstead (whichever side — schematic or P&ID — they're on). Using one of your private parts in a team project copies it into the team Codex.
On the Free plan only the read-only tools are available; edits need Pro or Student (whoami shows the plan). A Free user who is an editor/student or up in an active team or class can still edit that team's projects and Codex.
